title: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 + fused QKV ops and RoPE optimizations
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Motivation: Update our attention kernels to use FlashAttentionV2 primitives, add a fused QKV path and rotary/RoPE-aware kernel variants to improve throughput and reduce memory bandwidth for common generation workloads. This PR targets serving runtime hotspots observed in production: long-tail generation latency, KV cache memory churn, and suboptimal kernel selection for rotary embeddings. Changes include new CUDA kernels, scheduler hints for continuous batching, and small API-safe feature flags to toggle the new paths. Checklist: - [x] Implement FlashAttentionV2 wrapper and CUDA kernels - [x] Add fused QKV path for encoder/decoder blocks - [x] Implement RoPE-optimized kernels that avoid redundant rotations for cached prefixes - [x] Scheduler hints for sequence-length aware kernel selection (continuous batching) - [x] Unit tests for kernel correctness and equivalence with existing kernels - [x] Microbenchmarks across lengths and batch shapes - [x] Rollout feature flag with telemetry hooks - [x] Documentation for ops and perf notes (docs/perf/attention_kernels.md) Context: This work continues ENG-2012 and is a follow-up to earlier FlashAttention upgrades (see pr-20542 and pr-21789). In internal perf runs, the fused-QKV + RoPE-aware FlashAttentionV2 path reduces tail P99 latency by ~18% for autoregressive decoding at 2k tokens and improves throughput by ~22% at medium batch sizes on A100. The feature is guarded behind a runtime knob (ENABLE_FLASHATTN_V2) and a model metadata hint so we can safely roll it out per-customer. Risks and mitigations: - Numerical differences: we compare outputs with float32 epilogs and assert max-diff thresholds in unit tests. - Fallback correctness: the old kernel remains available and exercised in CI. - Memory behavior: KV-cache memory accounting updated to track the new fused buffers. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated pools -> staged ramp to hosted API models with telemetry watching lossless checks (token-level diffs, latency, OOMs). Related: ENG-2089 (scheduler improvements to support kernel hints).

Add unit tests and precision equivalence harnesses

merge_commit_message: Upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 wrapper, fused QKV, RoPE optimizations, scheduler hints, tests and docs
release_notes: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with a fused QKV execution path and RoPE-aware optimizations. Improves P99 latency and throughput for autoregressive decoding. Feature is behind ENABLE_FLASHATTN_V2 and can be toggled per-model. See docs/perf/attention_kernels.md for details and rollout notes.
performance_summary: Internal benchmarks: ~22% throughput improvement at common batch sizes, ~18% P99 latency reduction for long decoding runs (2k tokens) on A100. Memory usage slightly higher for fused buffers but overall KV-cache footprint reduced for prefix-heavy workloads.
notes: This PR is a follow-up to earlier flash attention upgrades (pr-20542, pr-21789)
Runtime knob ENABLE_FLASHATTN_V2 controls behavior; default in main remains off until canary completes
Telemetry covers kernel selection, fallbacks, and token-level diff sampling
